GAL.title: More chess games than stars in our galaxy #shorts
GAL.desc:
After five moves each there are 69,352,859,712,417 possible chess games. The Milky Way has somewhere between 100 and 400 billion stars. On the first move White has 20 choices and Black has 20 answers, so one move each already gives 400 games; two moves each give 197,281 and four moves each give 84,998,978,956. In 1950 Claude Shannon estimated about 10^120 possible games, far more than the roughly 10^80 atoms in the observable universe.
Free on iPhone and Android: joker-chess.com

Did you know chess was this big?

VAR.title: There are thousands of versions of chess #shorts
VAR.desc:
In Chess960 the back row starts in a random order, so memorized openings stop working; Bobby Fischer introduced it in 1996. In Crazyhouse every piece you capture switches sides and can be dropped back on the board. In Atomic chess every capture explodes and takes out the pieces around it, except pawns. In Three-check you win by giving check three times, in King of the Hill by walking your king to the centre. In Horde White has 36 pawns and nothing else against a normal army. In Racing Kings nobody can give check and the first king to reach the last row wins. And in Duck chess a rubber duck blocks a square after every move.
Free on iPhone and Android: joker-chess.com

TRK.title: The chess machine that fooled Napoleon #shorts
TRK.desc:
In 1770 Wolfgang von Kempelen showed a chess machine that started beating almost everyone who played it. It was called the Turk, and it toured Europe and America for 84 years. Benjamin Franklin played it in Paris and lost; Napoleon played it in Vienna and lost too. But it was a trick: a strong chess player was hiding inside the cabinet. The Turk burned in the fire at the Chinese Museum in Philadelphia in 1854, and soon after its secret was published.

RCE.title: Rice on a chessboard: the legend #shorts
RCE.desc:
Put one grain of rice on the first square of a chessboard, two on the second, and keep doubling. The last square alone needs 9,223,372,036,854,775,808 grains, and the whole board 18,446,744,073,709,551,615: more rice than the world grows in hundreds of years. An old legend says the man who invented chess asked a king for exactly this reward, and the king laughed at such a small request until his treasurers did the math.

KNT.title: The knight's tour: 64 squares, one knight #shorts
KNT.desc:
A knight can visit all 64 squares of a chessboard without landing on the same square twice. It's called a knight's tour, and people have been solving it for over a thousand years; the mathematician Leonhard Euler wrote a whole paper about it in 1759. The tour on screen is William Beverley's from 1848: written out as numbers, every row and every column adds up to 260. A tour that ends one jump away from its start is called closed, and there are 26,534,728,821,064 closed tours. In a real game a knight can need up to six moves to cross the board.

IMM.title: He gave away his queen and still won #shorts
IMM.desc:
London, 1851: Adolf Anderssen gave away a bishop, both his rooks and his queen against Lionel Kieseritzky, and still won, finishing with checkmate using only two knights and a bishop (23.Be7#). It was only a casual game, played during a break at the first international chess tournament. A few years later a chess writer named it the Immortal Game, and the name stuck.

MAG.title: Why Magnus Carlsen gave up the title #shorts
MAG.desc:
Magnus Carlsen won the World Championship five times, from 2013 to 2021, and then gave up the title without losing it. His last title match, in Dubai, started with five draws in a row. In 2022 he announced he would not defend it, saying he simply wasn't motivated to play another match. Since then he has played a lot of Freestyle chess, where the back row starts in a random order, and he even co-founded a new tour for it.

LNG.title: The longest chess game ever: 269 moves #shorts
LNG.desc:
With the rule that ends a game after 50 moves without a capture or a pawn move, the longest possible chess game is 5,949 moves. The longest game ever played in a tournament went 269 moves: Nikolić–Arsović, Belgrade 1989. It took over 20 hours and ended in a draw, in a rook and bishop against rook endgame, and right after it FIDE cut the move limit for that kind of endgame from 100 to 75. The longest World Championship game came in 2021: Carlsen beat Nepomniachtchi in 136 moves and almost eight hours.
Free on iPhone and Android: joker-chess.com

SPC.title: The first chess game in space ended in a draw #shorts
SPC.desc:
The first chess game ever played in space ended in a draw. In June 1970 the two cosmonauts on Soyuz 9, Andriyan Nikolayev and Vitaly Sevastyanov, played a team on the ground and sent every move by radio. They had White and opened with the Queen's Gambit, and after 35 moves, with a queen and five pawns each, the game was drawn (the whole game plays on the board). Fifty years later, cosmonauts on the International Space Station played grandmaster Sergey Karjakin, and that game was a draw too.

F1L.ig:
Chessboxing switches between rounds of chess and rounds of boxing: six of chess, five of boxing, and you win by checkmate or by knockout. The idea came from a 1992 French comic book by Enki Bilal; Dutch artist Iepe Rubingh turned it into a real sport in 2003 and fought as "the Joker".

Chess.com has duck chess, and atomic chess, where every capture blows up the pieces around it. Joker Chess, a new variant that's gaining popularity, keeps real chess and gives each player one Joker Move: a jump that can set up a fork or block a mate. No gloves needed. It's on the App Store and Google Play.

Chess or boxing first?
Joker Chess is free on iPhone and Android.
